kimchistew.name: Baek Jong-won's Pork Kimchi Stew
instructions: Cut the pork into bite-size pieces and stir-fry in oil over medium heat until the surface turns white.
Add the aged kimchi and stir-fry together for about 5 minutes until the kimchi softens.
Add sugar, minced garlic and red pepper flakes and stir-fry 1 more minute to build the base flavor.
Pour in the water and bring to a boil over high heat.
Once boiling, reduce to medium and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add sliced onion and simmer 5 more minutes.
Season with soup soy sauce and gochujang, adjusting to taste.
Add tofu in thick slices and simmer 5 minutes.
Finish with green onion and boil briefly.
Taste and adjust seasoning; add a pinch of MSG if you like.
Serve bubbling hot with rice.

doenjangstew.name: BBQ-House Doenjang Stew
instructions: Stir-fry the beef in a pot until browned.
Pour in the rice water and bring to a boil.
Dissolve the doenjang and a little gochujang into the broth.
Add diced zucchini and onion and simmer over medium heat for 10 minutes.
Add cubed tofu and minced garlic and simmer 5 more minutes.
Add sliced chili and green onion and boil briefly.
Let it thicken slightly — BBQ-house style is on the hearty side.
Serve hot with rice.

buldakramen.name: Buldak Ramen (Jirak-sil Style)
instructions: Thinly slice half an onion and fry in oil until lightly browned.
Add 400ml water, bring to a boil and cook the noodles.
When the noodles are 2/3 cooked, add the sauce packet and a slice of cheddar; stir and reduce.
With a little liquid left, plate it and top with egg yolk and mayonnaise.

blacktea.name: Classic Black Milk Tea
instructions: Bring the water to a boil and steep the tea bags for 3 minutes.
Remove the tea bags and dissolve the sugar.
Add the milk and heat gently — do not let it boil.
Turn off the heat right before boiling.
Strain into a cup and serve.

milktea.name: Rich Royal Milk Tea
instructions: Boil a small amount of water and steep the tea bags strongly for 5 minutes.
Add milk and warm over low heat for 3 minutes.
Sweeten with condensed milk.
Turn off the heat right before it boils.
Strain and serve hot.

ricecookercastella.name: Rice Cooker Castella
instructions: In a bowl, whisk together eggs, sugar, milk, oil, condensed milk and 3 drops of vanilla extract.
Sift in the cake flour and baking powder and mix gently until lump-free.
Lightly oil the rice cooker pot, pour in the batter, and tap the pot to release big bubbles.
Cook on the multi-steam setting for 40 minutes (or run the regular cook cycle twice).
Cool briefly, remove from the pot and slice.

dubaichocolate.name: Dubai Chocolate
instructions: Cut kataifi into 1cm pieces and toast in butter over medium-low heat for 8–10 minutes until golden and crisp; cool.
Mix the toasted kataifi with pistachio spread (add tahini to taste) to make the filling.
Melt the chocolate over a double boiler, coat the bottom and sides of a mold thinly, and chill 10 minutes.
Fill the chocolate shell with the pistachio-kataifi filling and press flat.
Cover with the remaining chocolate and chill 20+ minutes. The green cross-section is the money shot.

dujjonku.name: Dubai Chewy Cookie (Du-jjon-ku)
instructions: Toast chopped kataifi in butter until golden, then mix with pistachio spread for the filling.
Divide the dough into 50g portions, flatten, and wrap each around a spoonful of filling plus a marshmallow.
Bake at 175°C for 12–14 minutes until golden (air fryer: 160°C, 10–12 min).
Cool slightly and tear in half — stretchy marshmallow plus crunchy kataifi is the point.

butterdduk.name: Butter-Grilled Rice Cake
instructions: Melt half the butter in a pan over medium-low heat and add the rice cakes.
Grill 4–5 minutes per side until crisp and golden, adding the rest of the butter as you go.
Plate, drizzle with honey and dust with soybean powder. Crispy outside, chewy inside.

crookie.name: Crookie (Croissant Cookie)
instructions: Slice each croissant open sideways and spread half the cookie dough inside.
Top the croissant with the remaining dough and stud with chocolate chips.
Bake at 170°C for 12–15 minutes until the dough turns golden (air fryer: 160°C, 10 min).
Cool briefly and dust with powdered sugar — cookie outside, flaky layers inside.

yogurtbark.name: Frozen Yogurt Bark
instructions: Mix Greek yogurt with honey and spread 1cm thick on a lined tray.
Scatter sliced strawberries, blueberries and granola on top, pressing lightly.
Freeze 3+ hours, then snap into shards. A low-calorie ice cream stand-in.

pringleschoco.name: Pringles Chocolate Block
instructions: Finely chop the chocolate and melt with cream over a double boiler (or microwave in 30s bursts).
Leave the chips in the can and slowly pour the melted chocolate in, filling the gaps.
Chill the whole can for 4+ hours.
Cut the can away with scissors to reveal a chocolate cylinder. Slice for the cross-section shot.

mangosago.name: Mango Pomelo Sago
instructions: Boil sago pearls 12–15 minutes, then cover and rest until translucent. Rinse in cold water.
Blend 200g of mango with milk, coconut milk and sugar for the mango base.
Pour the base into bowls and add the sago pearls.
Top with diced mango and pomelo segments. Serve chilled — Hong Kong dessert classic.

bamtiramisu.name: Chestnut Tiramisu
instructions: Whip cream with sugar until stiff, fold in mascarpone, then fold in half the chopped chestnuts.
Dip ladyfingers in espresso for just 1 second per side and line the dish.
Layer: half the cream, dipped ladyfingers, then the remaining cream.
Chill 4+ hours, dust with cocoa and top with chestnuts — the convenience-store hit, homemade.

ubelatte.name: Ube Latte
instructions: Whisk ube powder with 30ml hot water into a smooth paste.
Mix the paste with condensed milk and spoon into the bottom of a glass.
Fill with ice and slowly pour in milk for a purple gradient. Stir before drinking.

pestoegg.name: Pesto Egg Toast
instructions: Spread a spoonful of pesto in a pan instead of oil and warm over medium-low heat.
When the pesto sizzles, crack the eggs on top and fry them in it.
Toast the bread, spread with a little more pesto, and slide the pesto eggs on.
Top with halved cherry tomatoes and grated parmesan — the TikTok pan-changer.

cottageflatbread.name: Cottage Cheese Flatbread
instructions: Blend cottage cheese, eggs, starch and salt until smooth.
Spread the batter thin on a parchment-lined baking tray.
Bake at 180°C for 25–30 minutes until the edges brown.
Cool, peel off, add toppings like avocado and roll it up. High-protein, low-carb bread swap.

cucumbersalad.name: TikTok Smashed Cucumber Salad
instructions: Smash the cucumbers with a rolling pin, cut into chunks, salt for 10 minutes and squeeze out water.
Mix soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, chili oil and garlic for the dressing.
Shake cucumbers and dressing together in a container. Sprinkle with sesame seeds.
Chill 30 minutes for best flavor — the 'whole cucumber, gone' viral salad.

carrotrape.name: Carottes Râpées Sandwich
instructions: Julienne the carrots, salt for 10 minutes and squeeze dry.
Toss with olive oil, lemon juice, mustard and honey (rest half a day in the fridge for best results).
Split the ciabatta and spread generously with cream cheese.
Pile in the carrot slaw. Keeps 5 days chilled — great for meal prep.

sundubuyeol.name: Silken Tofu Yeol Ramen
instructions: Boil 500ml water and cook the noodles with both soup packets for 2 minutes.
Add a whole block of silken tofu, breaking it into chunks; boil 1 more minute.
Add an egg and cook it soft; top with sliced green onion.
Baek Jong-won's hangover-friendly classic — the tofu soaks up the broth.

smashtaco.name: Smash Burger Taco
instructions: Shape beef into 50g balls, season with salt and pepper. Mix mayo, ketchup, mustard and chopped pickles for burger sauce.
Place a ball on a hot pan, press a tortilla on top, and smash hard so the patty fuses to it.
Sear the meat side 2–3 minutes until crusty, flip, top with cheese and cook 30 seconds.
Add lettuce, onion and sauce, fold in half. Smash-burger crust in taco form.

mararose.name: Mala Rosé Tteokbokki
instructions: Combine milk and cream in a pan; dissolve mala sauce, gochujang and sugar for the rosé base.
Add rice cakes and fish cakes and simmer 8–10 minutes, stirring, until the sauce thickens.
Balance the numbing mala heat with the creamy rosé; adjust mala sauce to taste.
Top with mozzarella and melt. The next act after the mala-tang craze.

eggjang.name: Cream Cheese Mayak Eggs
instructions: Boil eggs for 6 minutes 30 seconds, chill in ice water and peel.
Mix soy sauce, water and sugar; add chopped green onion and chili for the brine.
Put eggs and cubed cream cheese in a container, pour over the brine, and marinate 6+ hours.
Halve an egg over rice with cream cheese and brine — a salty-creamy rice thief.

smashedpotato.name: Crispy Smashed Potatoes
instructions: Boil baby potatoes in salted water for 15 minutes until tender.
Place on a baking tray and smash flat with the bottom of a cup — more cracks, more crunch.
Top with olive oil, minced garlic, parmesan and rosemary; roast at 220°C for 25 minutes until crispy.
Serve with sour cream and a drizzle of truffle oil. Crispy-edge potato perfection.

earlgreyhighball.name: Earl Grey Highball
instructions: Cold-steep an Earl Grey tea bag in 45ml whisky for 30 minutes — no longer, or it turns bitter.
Fill a highball glass with ice, add the infused whisky and honey syrup, and stir gently.
Pour tonic water slowly down the side of the glass to keep the fizz.
Garnish with a lemon slice. Tea highballs are the next step in home bartending.

mararosejjimdak.name: Mala Rosé Jjimdak (Braised Chicken)
instructions: Soak the glass noodles in lukewarm water for 30 minutes. Cut the potato and onion into chunks and slice the green onion diagonally.
Heat oil in a pan and sear the bite-sized chicken thigh over high heat until the surface turns opaque.
Add minced garlic and mala sauce, stir-fry for 1 minute, then mix in soy sauce, gochujang and sugar.
Add the potato, onion and 200ml water, cover and simmer over medium heat for 10 minutes.
Pour in the cream and milk, add the soaked noodles and simmer 5-7 more minutes until the sauce thickens.
Melt a slice of cheese on top and finish with green onion. Adjust the heat with the amount of mala sauce — add 50ml more milk if it's too spicy.

menbosha.name: Menbosha (Fried Shrimp Toast)
instructions: Trim the crusts and cut each slice into quarters — 16 pieces total. Freezing the bread briefly gives clean cuts.
Pat the shrimp completely dry and chop coarsely with the flat of a knife; a little texture is better than a paste.
Mix the shrimp with egg white, starch, cooking wine, salt and pepper, stirring one direction until sticky.
Mound the filling on one square of bread, cap with another and press the edges to seal.
Fry first at 130°C until pale gold, then rest for 3 minutes.
Raise the oil to 190°C and fry again for 10-20 seconds for a crisp shell.
Stir ketchup, vinegar, oyster sauce and sugar into a dipping sauce. Chef Lee Yeon-bok's signature dish.

kkanpunggi.name: Kkanpunggi (Sweet & Spicy Fried Chicken)
instructions: Cut the chicken into bite-size pieces and season with a little soy sauce and pepper for 10 minutes.
Mix egg and starch into a thick batter that coats without running.
Fry at 170°C, drain, then fry again at 190°C until crisp.
Premix soy sauce, vinegar, sugar and water — sour and sweet should carry equal weight.
Sauté minced garlic, sliced chili and green onion in oil until fragrant.
Pour in the sauce, reduce over high heat, then toss the fried chicken in quickly.
Almost no liquid should remain. Adjust heat with the pepper flakes.

chamchimayo.name: Tuna Mayo Rice Bowl
instructions: Press the tuna hard and drain every drop of oil — skip this and the whole bowl turns greasy.
Slice half the onion and finely dice the other half.
Sauté the garlic and sliced onion in oil until translucent.
Add soy sauce, sugar and cooking wine; kill the heat once it bubbles.
Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt and cook into a soft scramble.
Mix the drained tuna with the diced onion, mayonnaise and a little pepper.
Layer the onion sauce, tuna mayo and scrambled egg over rice; finish with mayo, seaweed flakes and shredded perilla.

gajidupbap.name: Chinese-Style Eggplant Rice Bowl
instructions: Cut the eggplant into batons, soak in salted water for 5 minutes and squeeze dry — it absorbs far less oil this way.
Heat chili oil and fry the garlic and green onion until fragrant.
Add the ground pork and stir-fry over high heat until it changes colour.
Add the eggplant and stir-fry until the surface softens.
Pour in oyster sauce, soy sauce, sugar and water and simmer 2-3 minutes.
Thicken with the starch slurry and spoon over rice.

spoonpasta.name: Spoon Pasta
instructions: Snap the spaghetti in half and boil one minute under the package time — short strands are what make it spoonable.
Crisp the bacon in olive oil, then sauté the garlic and onion.
Halve the cherry tomatoes, add them and crush with a spatula to build the sauce.
Loosen with pasta water, add the noodles and toss for 30 seconds.
Grate in the cheese off the heat and fold it through.
Serve in a deep bowl with basil — eaten with a spoon, Chef Choi Hyun-seok style.

ganjangbutter.name: Soy Butter Egg Rice
instructions: Melt the butter and fry the sliced green onion to flavour the fat.
Crack in the eggs and fry sunny-side up until the whites crisp at the edges.
Drizzle soy sauce and sugar around the rim of the pan so they caramelise — that aroma is the whole point.
Slide the eggs and sauce over hot rice, add sesame oil and seaweed flakes, and mix.

ochazuke.name: Salmon Ochazuke
instructions: Steep the green tea bag in hot water for 2 minutes for a slightly strong brew.
Put warm rice in a bowl and drape the smoked salmon over it.
Add a circle of soy sauce and a dab of wasabi in the centre.
Pour the tea until the rice is half submerged; top with seaweed, chives and sesame. Good for a hangover too.

kimchicream.name: Kimchi Cream Pasta
instructions: Shake the seasoning off the kimchi and chop it small — the more sour, the better.
Boil the spaghetti one minute under the package time.
Sauté bacon, garlic and onion in olive oil.
Add the kimchi and fry a full 3 minutes to cook off the sharp acidity; skip this and it never marries with the cream.
Pour in the cream and milk and reduce over low heat for 5 minutes.
Add the pasta and pasta water to set the consistency, then grate cheese over the top.

garlicshrimp.name: Garlic Butter Oyster-Sauce Shrimp
instructions: Pat the shrimp dry and season with pepper — leftover water will steam instead of sear.
Melt the butter and fry the garlic slowly until golden.
Turn the heat up and cook the shrimp for 2 minutes until the surface turns pink.
Add oyster sauce, soy sauce and sugar and toss for just 30 seconds; longer and the shrimp turns rubbery.
Finish with sliced chili and green onion.

spamkimchibokkeum.name: Spam Kimchi Fried Rice
instructions: Dice the Spam and sear it in a dry pan until browned, letting the fat render out.
Fry the green onion in that fat, then stir-fry the chopped kimchi for 3 minutes.
Add gochujang, sugar and kimchi brine and fry one more minute.
Add the rice and press it into the kimchi with the spatula until evenly coated.
Return the Spam, drizzle sesame oil and fold through.
Top with a fried egg and seaweed flakes.
